newsitem.title: USA: CME offers to delay trade on Taiwan stock index.
newsitem.headline: CME offers to delay trade on Taiwan stock index.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) has offered to delay the launch of futures and options trade on the Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index until January 15, 1997, a CME spokeswoman said Thursday.
"We've made a good-faith proposal to the chairman of Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission that we would delay the launch until January 15," the spokeswoman said.

She said the CME offered to delay the launch, originally scheduled for November, because of concerns of Taiwan regulators that the introduction of futures and options would increase volatility in Taiwan's stock market.
"They expressed specific concerns to us which we addressed when we made this proposal to them," she said.
The Taiwan Stock Exchange is planning to open its futures exchange in July 1997, several months earlier than planned.

However, regulatory approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission is still pending for CME futures and options on the Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index. Once the contracts are approved, they will be listed in the CME's Growth and Emerging Markets division.
Dow Jones & Co Inc licensed the CME to trade contracts on the Dow Jones Taiwan Stock Index in September.

The CME had originally selected the Taiwan 100 Index as the basis for its futures and options trade, and had applied for regulatory approval in May. The Dow Jones Taiwan index comprises 113 of the largest stocks traded on the Taiwan exchange.
The spokeswoman said the CME also asked Taiwan's Stock Exchange for an information-sharing agreement.
"It is information on surveillance that we would be sharing on an as-needed basis upon request," she said. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
